test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 17 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: John bought a laptop at 25% discount on the marked price. If he paid Rs. 28,473 for the laptop, what was its marked price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The fractional value of 25% discount = 1/4

Let Marked Price (MP) = 4 units, then Discount = 1 unit.

Selling Price (SP) = 4 − 1 = 3 units.

Since 3 units = Rs. 28,473 → 1 unit = Rs. 28,473 ÷ 3 = Rs. 9,491.

MP = 4 units = 4 × Rs. 9,491 = Rs. 37,964.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 37,964.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount = 25%

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 28,473

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 
 SP = Rs. 28,473 (75%)
 
 
 Discount (25%)

 

 Marked Price (100%) = ?

**Calculation:**

⇒ 28,473 = MP × (100 − 25) ÷ 100

⇒ 28,473 = MP × 75 ÷ 100

⇒ 28,473 = MP × 3 ÷ 4

⇒ MP = (28,473 × 4) ÷ 3

⇒ MP = 9,491 × 4

⇒ MP = 37,964

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 37,964.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the equivalent single discount is [x + y − (x × y ÷ 100)]%.

Relationship between MP and CP

The direct ratio between Marked Price and Cost Price is given by: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Mark-up Percentage

It is the percentage by which the cost price is increased to set the marked price. Mark-up % = (MP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.
